chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from al-ʿAbbās, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from some of his companions, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, he said:
"When the water is the measure of two qullahs, nothing renders it impure; and the two qullahs are two jars."

So this is a mursal report, and it is possible that it was issued by way of taqiyyah due to its agreement with the doctrine of many of the ʿāmmah. It is also possible that the intended meaning in it is what we have mentioned in other than this report, namely that the measure of the two qullahs is the measure of the kurr, because that is not objectionable, since the qullah in language is the large jar; and on this basis there is no contradiction between the reports.

key_terms.جَرَّتَانِ: two jars, explaining the meaning of the two qullahs
key_terms.خَبَرٌ مُرْسَلٌ: a report with a missing link in the sanad/isnad
key_terms.قُلَّتَيْنِ: two large jars, a volumetric measure mentioned as a purity threshold
key_terms.ٱلتَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation for protection, here as a possible reason for the wording of the report
key_terms.ٱلْأَخْبَارِ: reports or hadiths, among which reconciliation is being proposed
key_terms.ٱلْعَامَّةِ: the general Sunni majority, whose view may align with the report
key_terms.ٱلْكُرِّ: kurr, the recognized legal measure of a large quantity of water
key_terms.ٱلْمَاءُ: water, the substance whose legal ruling is being discussed

ai.seo_question: How does Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām reconcile the hadith of two qullahs with narrations about kurr water?
ai.summary: This report discusses the legal threshold of water that does not become najis through contact with impurity, identifying it as the amount of two qullahs. The accompanying scholarly note explains that the report is mursal and may reflect taqiyyah, or else may be reconciled with other narrations by understanding two qullahs as equivalent to the kurr measure.
